memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "They made upright frames of acacia wood for the tabernacle. Each frame was ten cubits long and a cubit and a half wide, with two projections set parallel to each other. They made all the frames of the tabernacle in this way." - Exod 36:20-22 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Beneath all those beautiful curtains stood a skeleton of plain acacia wood.

Acacia is a desert tree — hard, dense, resistant to insects and rot. Not decorative. Not valuable. But it could stand in harsh conditions for years without breaking down.

Structure matters. The gorgeous embroidered curtains would have collapsed into a heap without these upright frames holding everything in place.

The same is true in the Christian life. We tend to prize the visible things — the moving worship, the powerful sermon, the emotional experience. But what actually holds a life upright over decades is unglamorous structure: regular Scripture reading, honest prayer, committed church membership, accountability, simple obedience repeated.

Jesus described the wise builder as the one who dug down deep and laid the foundation on rock, so that when the flood came the house could not be shaken (Luke 6:47-48). The digging is not the exciting part. It is the part that decides everything.

Notice too the phrase "set parallel to each other" and "all the frames in this way." Consistency. Every frame made to the same pattern, so they would fit together and hold.

What is holding your life upright when the curtains of feeling come down?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What structures currently hold your faith upright?
2. Have you built on experience rather than on solid habits?
3. What is one practice you need to establish and keep?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, build strong structure into my life. Let my faith stand when feelings fail. Amen.
